message.content: 獅子（Felidae）與斑馬（Equidae）的最近共同祖先屬於「Laurasiatheria」這一大類，距今約在七千萬年前。那時候的祖先是一種小型、可能以昆蟲為食的哺乳動物，體形相對簡單，並不具備現代貓科或馬科所特有的特殊適應性。隨著時間演化，分支出不同的路徑：一條發展成了貓科（最終演化出獵食性的獅子），另一條則演化成了奇蹄目（最終形成像斑馬這樣的大型草食動物）。因此，雖然兩者現在生活方式截然不同，但它們共享的是早期哺乳類的共同祖先，而不是更近的直接親緣關係。

The user asks: "獅子和斑馬的共同祖先是什麼？" which translates to "What is the common ancestor of lions and zebras?" They want an answer about evolutionary biology. We can provide a concise explanation: both belong to order Carnivora? Actually lions are Felidae (family), zebras are Equidae (family). Both are mammals, but their last common ancestor would be at some level. Lions are in suborder Feliformia, zebras in Perissodactyla. Their last common ancestor would be a mammalian ancestor from the Eutherian lineage. But maybe they want the most recent common ancestor: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or more specifically, the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be something like the last common ancestor of the clade that includes Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria group. So we could say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, probably insectivore-like mammal that lived around 70 million years ago, part of the early Laurasiatherians.
